title: Schema-driven adapter for legacy callback-style tool invocations
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: We have two dominant invocation patterns in customer workloads: (1) OpenAI-style 'tool' calls that expect a single structured JSON response and well-defined function signatures, and (2) older 'callback/legacy function' integrations where the model emits partial outputs and the client expects a streaming callback envelope or an ad-hoc parameter marshalling format. These diverge on naming, parameter serialization, streaming boundaries, error surfaces, and provenance metadata.

Proposal: Implement a schema-driven adapter layer in the runtime that can: (a) surface a canonical operation registry (name, input schema, output schema, stability signals), (b) apply deterministic name and parameter translations between legacy function shapes and OpenAI-style tool signatures, (c) translate streaming partials into a streaming envelope that preserves token-level provenance and can be reassembled into structured outputs, and (d) provide configurable fallback behaviors (best-effort mapping, fail-open with telemetry, or strict-reject).

Key user scenarios addressed: structured-output-first tools calling legacy callbacks; streaming-first legacy integrations that must be presented as tools to newer clients; gradual migration where both surfaces are exposed simultaneously for a customer; automated rollback if mapping causes semantic regressions.

Core components: registry (YAML/JSON manifest per customer or global), adapter runtime module (translation rules + validation), streaming envelope protocol (sentinel frames + schema checkpoints), compatibility header promotion (X-Compat-Tool / X-Compat-Version), and telemetry/qa harness (shadow-invocation + diffing to detect output drift).

Trade-offs: 1) Latency vs fidelity: adding translation/validation introduces processing latency for synchronous calls; mitigation: translation cache and route-level opt-outs. 2) Consistency vs adoption friction: strict schema validation prevents subtle regressions but blocks existing clients; mitigation: phased rollout with 'per-route permissive' flag. 3) Complexity surface area: more tests, more observability required — we propose automated regression/eval jobs as part of CI for any adapter change.

Acceptance criteria: adapter can translate 3 canonical legacy callback patterns (streaming-chunked JSON, newline-delimited key=value, and single JSON blob) into OpenAI-style tool responses with >=95% schema-validate pass rate on a representative dataset; streaming envelopes preserve original token provenance for replay; end-to-end latency increase <10ms P50 for non-streaming paths; metrics and rollback hooks are plumbed into Console rollout controls.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff: scoped canonical legacy patterns with PM (Priya) and Design (Noah). Captured three example customers in Confluence: /confluence/redwood/tool-interop/legacy-patterns

2026-03-05 — Prototype: initial adapter implemented as a transparent middleware that performs name normalization and basic JSON->schema projection. Benchmarked extra latency ~8ms median. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824

2026-03-07 — Design review: agreed on streaming envelope structure (frames: meta/checkpoint/token_chunk/end). Noah requested explicit 'schema-checkpoint' frames so client UIs can show partial structured validation.

2026-03-09 — PM feedback (Priya): require per-customer registry override and a migration mode that supports 'shadow-invocation' where the adapter runs translations but does not modify live responses while we collect diffs.

2026-03-11 — Engineering spike: implemented token provenance by tagging chunks with provenance headers (compat-tool, invocation-id, chunk-index). Added opt-in header X-Compat-Mode: shadow. Integration tests added under runtime/interop_tests.

2026-03-13 — Security review request opened: https://redwood.secure/reviews/SEC-2026-47 — main items: ensure no accidental leakage of internal diagnostics into client streaming frames; sanitized telemetry paths. Security flagged a need to strip stack traces from error frames.

2026-03-14 — Current: PR in flight for adapter and streaming-envelope. Running canary on dedicated cluster 'compat-canary-1' with two customers; collecting schema-violation alerts. Next: implement rollback hook exposed in Console rollout UI and add more regression evals.
decision_log: Use schema-first translation: canonical JSON schemas are the single source of truth for mapping decisions (decision made 2026-03-05)
Streaming envelope will include explicit checkpoint frames so downstream consumers (Console/UI) can render partial validated structure (decision made 2026-03-07)
Introduce 'shadow-invocation' mode for safe validation before live migration (decision made 2026-03-09)
Telemetry will include translation-diff metrics and a per-route 'compat-failure-rate' metric for rollout gating (decision made 2026-03-11)
next_steps: Merge PR after security sign-off and add rollout toggle in Console
Run 2-week canary with shadow-invocation enabled for selected customers
Create migration guide + code snippets for customers (examples: Node/TS client, Python streaming consumer)
Add automated regression evals comparing legacy vs translated outputs and wire into Optimize quality alerts
